title: Vesuvius Challenge: first letters read from an unopened Herculaneum scroll
summary: For the first time, a complete word (‘porphyras’, purple) was read from inside a never-opened carbonized scroll; a model trained on crack patterns yielded 13 letters independently and unanimously annotated by papyrologists. The letters are faint and lack context; other readings are not ruled out.

evidence.tested: A model trained on crack patterns produced 13 letters, which papyrologists independently annotated with varying confidence; the page links only to code and no paper.
evidence.unknown: The letters are faint and lack context, word boundaries are unclear, and the page states other readings are not ruled out and the papyrological team was still investigating.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models trained on ink crackle patterns (and a second model with pseudo-labeling) read letters from the scroll.
